title: DOW-UAP-PR166 (Release 08, Middle East 2020): small boat and wake?

content:
• #1

Source: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/1030270/dow-uap-pr166-unresolved-uap-report-middle-east-2020 (PURSUE Release 08, 20 Nov 2026)

External Quote:

00:00-00:09: An area of contrast enters the sensor field-of-view from the right edge of the frame, proceeding from right to left. 00:10-00:20: The sensor pans and cycles the level of magnification to track the area of contrast, keeping it generally within the center of the frame.

The sensor looks like it's pointed down at the sea at a shallow angle. There are wave crests along the bottom of the frame. The "area of contrast" sits on that surface and leaves a long bright trail behind it, on the side it's moving away from.

At about 8.5 s the trail bends as the object turns. To me that looks like a small boat and its wake in IR, not something in the air. A bird skimming the water is possible, but a trail that stays put and curves fits a wake better.

EDIT: As RobertBillyBob and John J. point out below, the "object" and "trail" are most likely warm spots on a larger ship (near its bow), not a small boat and wake. The feature AARO describes is a different one; see John J.'s post #3.

Last edited: Today at 9:24 AM

  • #3

I think the OP might be looking at a different feature to the one described by AARO.

External Quote:

Video description:
00:00-00:09: An area of contrast enters the sensor field-of-view from the right edge of the frame, proceeding from right to left.
00:10-00:20: The sensor pans and cycles the level of magnification to track the area of contrast, keeping it generally within the center of the frame.

(AARO report on DVIDS website https://www.dvidshub.net/video/1030270/dow-uap-pr166-unresolved-uap-report-middle-east-2020)

What appears to be some sort of structure is probably a ship.
(The outline here is very approximate- a suggestion. The right edge of the bridge/ superstructure is probably too far to the right; I think I misidentified unconnected brighter features as features on the ship).

The "object" and "trail behind it" identified in the OP are likely warm points or areas of (IR) reflection towards the vessel's bow.
Their position doesn't really match the AARO description.

What I think is the feature of interest enters right of frame and travels to the left as described by AARO.
It briefly sems to travel behind, and is obscured by, what might be a bridge structure or something similar on the (I think probable) ship.

Edited to add, after the feature passes the ship it briefly appears to be two small bright features very close to each other horizontally.
If I had to guess at the moment I'd say it might be a powered aircraft.

External Quote:

filmed in the Middle East in 2020, a tiny object glowing white hot on infrared appears to fly across the bow of a warship.

Daily Mail, quoted in post #2.
If the feature is being obscured by the ship's bridge/ superstructure, it is behind the ship and not flying across its bow.

  • #4

@RobertBillyBob @John J. You're both right, thanks. With the contrast turned up there's a faint ship outline, and what I called the object and its wake sit on it. So they're most likely warm spots on the ship, near the bow as John J. says, not a small boat.

I've added an EDIT to my first post. The feature AARO describes, coming in from the right and passing behind the structure, looks like the one to follow.

  • #5

If this object is a bird, it is a large, fast one.

It may instead be a drone - presumably an enemy drone, unless the people filming the clip were kept completely out of the loop, which is entirely possible

  • #6

The person/ people submitting the clip to AARO might not be the people who took the footage or who had responsibility for interpreting it.
I think this is a weak point in the reporting system. Imagery which was understood or considered to be of no consequence at the time can be reported by others who have access to that imagery but perhaps not other information that might explain it.
